notes.text: Undated handwritten page: formula (11) defines X*=X minus circled T=(X minus T) union dotted T and calls it a closed part of X. The proposition lists a), b), b-prime), and c) as equivalent conditions for a given 0<lambda<1; it then names a strict conic neighbourhood. A transverse note proposes germs of larger neighbourhoods. Two corollaries assert an ambient-frontier identity and strictness of scaled neighbourhoods. This is a transcription-only content account, not a proof of those statements.

Local source distinctions: every ordinary T has one cap and stem, without a further bar. Hollow-circle interior and filled-dot boundary symbols are distinct. Circumflexes are retained in cônique/côniques where visible; the author’s lui-= abbreviation is not expanded. Condition b has a clear final closing parenthesis but no separate live opening arc. Missing final stops after the strict definition and the last corollary are preserved. The additional triangular group in the second corollary is retained with token/state/caret uncertainty.

Conditional root counterexample to the opening closedness claim, using the literal cone-neighbourhood interpretation supplied by root (the first reader did not inspect another leaf): let X=([0,1]×{0}) union ({3/8}×[0,1]), Y={(0,0)}, T=[0,1/2]×{0}, dotted T={(1/2,0)}, with scalar action lambda·(t,0)=(lambda t,0). T is a closed neighbourhood of Y carrying the absolute cone structure. Its circled part is [0,1/2)×{0}. Therefore X*=X minus circled T omits the junction q=(3/8,0), but contains points (3/8,s) for s>0 tending to q. X* is not closed in X, although the displayed set identity (11) remains valid. The literal sentence “c’est une partie fermée de X” is unchanged.

Conditional root counterexample to the proposed equivalence in the same space, at the proposition parameter lambda=1/2: condition a holds under the collar interpretation supplied by root, since dotted T has the collar [1/2,1]×{0} inside X*. Condition c holds with T-prime=[0,1]×{0}; then T=lambda T-prime and the scalar structures agree. Condition b fails because every homeomorphism of X fixes its unique valence-three point q=(3/8,0), whereas q lies in T but not lambda T=[0,1/4]×{0}. Consequently b-prime, which adds requirements to b, also fails. These facts refute equivalence under the stated literal hypotheses; no corrected equivalence is claimed.

Qualification of the first frontier corollary in the same conditional example: the ambient frontier of T is {q,(1/2,0)}, whereas dotted T is only {(1/2,0)}. Thus if strictness is assigned by either a or c as proposed equivalent criteria, that corollary fails in this example. This does not assert failure under a definition that independently requires b. The obstruction is missing control of the ambient openness of circled T, not an error to be silently repaired in the transcription. No general sufficiency theorem for an added hypothesis is proved here.

The root supplied the example and its cone/collar interpretation; reader_a rechecked the coordinate membership, limiting vertical points, and valence obstruction in the course of recording it. Other-page definitions were not independently read. The second corollary and the marginal germ proposal are preserved without a separate general proof. The terminal marginal -R_{>0}-like group remains a reading doubt and receives no mathematical expansion.

Layout and hand attribution: the transverse note overlaps rectangular frames of main On dit and Corollaire text, which are not duplicated as marginal words. The small arrow-like stroke above the raised second-corollary T is the descender of the preceding frontière f, not an independent insertion arrow. The lower portion of the leaf is blank apart from thin foliation 14, whose hand attribution is indeterminate.
